xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5242: Bot connector: relay failures report as retryable 'direct connection failed'; add a no-webrtc-egress error and TURN health check

plan.title: Bot connector: relay failures report as retryable 'direct connection failed'; add a no-webrtc-egress error and TURN health check
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One incident fix with five linked requirements. The code spans three source subsystems (src/lib for the transport and connector, src/dashboard for one route, src/cli for one doctor row); the rest of the 25 files are their tests and five doc files, and each top-level doc file counts as its own subsystem. The TURN health check is not a separate feature: the no-webrtc-egress next text and docs point to it as the only way to tell a relay outage from a blocked bot, so shipping either half alone leaves the operator guidance wrong.

narratives.Problem: A bot connector that cannot open a WebRTC channel reports status retry, code machine-unreachable, with the text 'direct connection failed', even when the relay (TURN) leg failed and a retry cannot help. RtcTransport labels every route's failure 'direct connection' (rtc-transport.ts:389), pair.ts:239-242 maps every relay failure to machine-unreachable, connect-output.ts:40 makes that retryable, and neither side logs how many ICE candidates it gathered, so 'no TURN candidate' cannot be told apart from 'TURN down'. The last successful relay connection was weeks ago, so TURN health is unproven.
narratives.Proposal: Name the route in every RtcTransport error. Tally candidates by kind on both sides and log the tallies on the offer, the answer and every state line. On a relay dial whose ICE list names a TURN URL but which gathered zero 'typ relay' candidates, fail at once with ChannelOpenError('unreachable', ..., { cause: 'no-relay-candidate' }) and send no offer. Map that cause to a new non-retryable status code no-webrtc-egress in both the pairing path (pair.ts) and the existing-pairing verify path (ConnectorLink + connect.ts). Add an on-demand relay check: a lib probe that gathers relay candidates once, a dashboard route POST /api/anywhere/relay-check that fetches TURN credentials through the live directory client, and a pan doctor 'TURN relay' row that calls it. Document the code, the log lines, the route and the doctor row, and add a changelog entry. Full detail: .pan/drafts/PAN-5242.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to the phone dialer (packages/anywhere-channel/src/dial-machine.ts) or its error messages.
- No new ChannelOpenErrorCode value; the cause rides detail.cause.
- No relay check inside GET /api/anywhere/status, no background or periodic TURN check, and no Settings UI for it.
- No change to werift, to relayIceServers ordering, or to the one-TURN-URL limit.
- No change to which existing connect codes are retry (network, machine-offline, machine-unreachable, verify-failed stay retry).
- No fix for the responder dropping candidates that arrive before the session is registered.
- No change to pan mcp connector serve beyond the route-labelled lastError text.
- The CLI never opens its own directory socket for the relay check.
- No log line, error or doctor row carries SDP, candidate text, TURN credentials, keys or tokens.

autoDecisions.summary: The no-relay-candidate cause is carried in ChannelOpenError.detail.cause with code 'unreachable'; no new ChannelOpenErrorCode.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every existing consumer (link supervisor, LinkAgent, phone) switches on the code; keeping 'unreachable' leaves them unchanged while the connector reads the cause.

autoDecisions.summary: RtcTransport fails a relay dial at once when it gathered zero relay candidates, and sends no offer; this applies to the dashboard's machine-to-machine and approval relay dials too.
autoDecisions.rationale: werift finishes gathering inside setLocalDescription (measured: 0 candidates, 4 ms to 8.0 s), so the count is final; failing there is faster and deterministic, and gathering ends before the 10 s and 15 s relay open budgets.

autoDecisions.summary: Count 'typ relay' candidates, not the total.
autoDecisions.rationale: Measured: werift gathers host candidates in relay mode when its list has no usable TURN server (34 candidates, 0 relay), so a total would hide the failure.

autoDecisions.summary: The health check is on demand: POST /api/anywhere/relay-check plus a pan doctor 'TURN relay' row, silent unless signed in with the relay plan; warn, never error.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue allows pan doctor or the Anywhere status; the status route is polled, so a TURN allocation per poll is wasteful, and the relay is optional reachability.

autoDecisions.summary: The phone dialer's 'direct connection' strings are out of scope; FR-1 is read as every error RtcTransport and the connector produce.
autoDecisions.rationale: The incident, the bot connector and every line the issue cites are the Node RtcTransport; dial-machine.ts is a separate browser package shipped inside the mobile app, with pinned messages, and no phone report is involved.

autoDecisions.summary: callDashboard gains an optional signal so the doctor row can bound its two calls (3 s and 25 s).
autoDecisions.rationale: Without it a hung relay check would keep pan doctor waiting; the change is additive.

autoDecisions.summary: The responder keeps its exact 'rtc session <s> answered' line and adds a separate 'answer to' tally line.
autoDecisions.rationale: Existing tests pin the answered line (rtc-transport.test.ts:207,337).

autoDecisions.summary: Critique response: no-webrtc-egress stays a non-retryable error, but its next text says 'the usual cause is …' and sends the user to pan doctor on the machine to rule out a relay outage before switching to Public MCP.
autoDecisions.rationale: The dialer cannot tell blocked egress from a TURN outage or refused allocation; the issue requires a distinct non-retryable code, and status error makes the bot hand the decision to the user instead of looping.

autoDecisions.summary: Critique response: requestIceServers rejects with a typed IceServersRefusedError only for a directory error frame; timeouts become the relay check state 'unanswered'.
autoDecisions.rationale: A timeout is not a refusal; the doctor must not tell the operator overdeck.ai refused credentials when it never answered.

metadata.acJustification: Five ACs: the abort, close and setup-error paths each need their own observable message check.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-1. In src/lib/anywhere/channel/rtc-transport.ts add `export type RtcRoute = 'direct' | 'relay'` and `routeOf(relay)`. RtcDialAbortedError takes `route: RtcRoute = 'direct'` and its message becomes `${route} connection aborted`; pass routeOf(opts.relay) at the two throws in dial() and routeOf(entry.relay) in awaitOpen. awaitOpen's two errors become `${route} data channel closed before it opened` and `${route} connection ${state}`. Add the test described in WI-1; keep the existing toBeInstanceOf(RtcDialAbortedError) checks. Also (critique response) wrap the whole body of create() in try/catch and rethrow withRoute(routeOf(relay), error): a module helper that prefixes '<route> connection: ' once (skipping messages that already start with '<route> connection'), rebuilds a ChannelOpenError with the same code and detail, and wraps anything else in a plain Error with { cause }. Import ChannelOpenError from '@overdeck/anywhere-channel' here. Keep the existing closeEntry(entry) on an offer failure.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-3. Import ChannelOpenError from '@overdeck/anywhere-channel' and turnUrlRank from './relay-ice-servers.js'. Export NO_RELAY_CANDIDATE_CAUSE = 'no-relay-candidate', isNoRelayCandidate(error) (ChannelOpenError with detail.cause equal to it) and firstTurnUrl(servers). In create(), after the offer tally log line and before sendLocalDescription: when relay is true, firstTurnUrl(iceServers) is not null and entry.gathered.counts.relay === 0, closeEntry(entry) and throw new ChannelOpenError('unreachable', `relay connection: gathered no TURN relay candidate from ${turnUrl}; the TURN server could not be reached from this host or refused the allocation`, { cause: NO_RELAY_CANDIDATE_CAUSE }). A relay list with no TURN URL does not fail fast. Tests use the closed loopback port turn:127.0.0.1:1?transport=tcp (real timers, about 4 ms). withRoute (from route-named-errors) leaves this error and its cause unchanged because its message already starts with 'relay connection'.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-7. New src/lib/anywhere/channel/relay-probe.ts exporting RELAY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS = 12_000, the RelayCheckResponse union (skipped / refused / unanswered / ok / failed), RelayProbeResult, RelayProbePeer and probeRelayCandidate(servers, deps). Order the list with relayIceServers, pick turnUrl with firstTurnUrl (from rtc-transport.ts); no TURN URL returns failed with detail 'the relay list has no TURN server' and creates no peer. narrative.Action: PRD WI-9. callDashboard accepts an optional signal and passes it to fetch. New doctor-anywhere-relay.ts re-declares CheckResult structurally (like doctor-fly.ts) and exports checkAnywhereRelay({ call }): GET /api/anywhere/status with a 3 s AbortController deadline (unreachable, aborted or non-200 → []); if directory.state is not 'online' or relay is null → []; POST /api/anywhere/relay-check with a 25 s deadline; map ok → ok row 'Gathered <n> relay candidate(s) via <turnUrl> in <ms> ms', failed with turnUrl → warn with the fix naming the TURN host:port (parse: drop the turns:/turn: scheme and any ?query; no port means 5349 for turns:, 3478 for turn:), failed with turnUrl null → warn 'overdeck.ai sent relay credentials with no TURN server: <detail>' with fix 'This is an overdeck.ai service problem, not this machine's network. Report it.', refused → warn 'overdeck.ai refused relay credentials: <detail>', unanswered → warn 'overdeck.ai did not send relay credentials: <detail>', skipped → [], deadline → warn 'The relay check did not answer within 25 s', POST throws before the deadline → warn 'The relay check failed: <message>', other status → warn 'The relay check answered HTTP <n>'. callDashboard wraps every fetch failure (an abort included) in DashboardUnreachableError, so decide the deadline row from the item's own controller.signal.aborted, never from the error type. Row name 'TURN relay', never 'error'. Register it in doctor.ts after the checkFlyToken line with one import and one line.
